h1: Marking Classified Information Training Quiz & Practice Questions
subhead: Take a free practice quiz or get instant, explained answers to Marking Classified Information questions — portion marks, banner lines, and classification authority blocks, without the guesswork.
metaTitle: Marking Classified Information Training Quiz & Practice Questions | Cambo
metaDescription: Free Marking Classified Information quiz and practice questions with instant, explained answers. Banner lines, portion markings, classification authority blocks, and dissemination controls.
whyItWorks: Marking questions live in the details — telling a banner line apart from a portion mark, or knowing exactly which elements belong in a classification authority block — and it's easy to transpose one for the other under time pressure. Cambo reads the exact marking example on your screen and explains which element is which and why.

sampleQuestions.q: What is the purpose of a banner marking on a classified document?
options: It identifies who is authorized to read the document
It identifies the highest overall classification level of the entire document, and appears at the top and bottom of every page
It records the date the document was created
It lists every person who has ever accessed the document
sampleQuestions.a: A banner marking identifies the highest overall classification level of the entire document and appears at the top and bottom of every page — it reflects the most sensitive information anywhere in the document, not just that page.

sampleQuestions.q: A paragraph in a classified document begins with "(S)" before the first word. What does this portion marking indicate?
options: The entire document is classified SECRET
That specific paragraph is classified SECRET, independent of what the overall document's banner marking says
The paragraph was written by a Senior official
The paragraph has been approved for public release
sampleQuestions.a: It means that specific paragraph is classified SECRET. Portion markings apply to individual sections — a document's overall banner marking reflects its highest classified portion, but each portion is still marked according to its own classification level.

sampleQuestions.q: Which of the following must appear in a classification authority block?
options: Classified By, Derived From, and Declassify On
Author's home address and personal phone number
A list of every prior draft of the document
The document's page count and file size
sampleQuestions.a: A classification authority block must include "Classified By" (who classified it), "Derived From" (the source or guide used), and "Declassify On" (when or under what event the classification ends).

sampleQuestions.q: What does the dissemination control marking "NOFORN" mean?
options: The document cannot be released to foreign nationals, regardless of its classification level
The document is not classified and can be shared freely
The document must be destroyed within 24 hours
The document has been formally declassified
sampleQuestions.a: "NOFORN" means "Not Releasable to Foreign Nationals" — it restricts dissemination to foreign nationals regardless of the document's classification level, and it's a control separate from the classification itself.

sampleQuestions.q: You're creating a working paper that contains classified information and expect to keep it for reference for less than 180 days. How should it be marked?
options: It doesn't need to be marked since it's only a working paper
With the highest classification level it contains, the words "WORKING PAPER," and the date it was created
Only with the author's name and no classification marking
As UNCLASSIFIED until a final version is produced
sampleQuestions.a: Mark it with its highest classification level, the words "WORKING PAPER," and the date created — if it's retained beyond 180 days or transmitted outside the originating agency, it must then be marked as a finished document instead.

sampleQuestions.q: A short portion of a classified document contains no classified information at all. How should that portion be marked?
options: It should be left without any portion marking
With "(U)" immediately preceding it, indicating that specific portion is unclassified
With the same marking as the highest classified portion in the document
With "(TS)" to be safe
sampleQuestions.a: An unclassified portion within an otherwise classified document is marked with "(U)" immediately preceding it — every portion needs its own marking, including the ones that aren't classified at all.

faqs.q: How often is Marking Classified Information training required?
faqs.a: Annually, typically alongside Derivative Classification training, for anyone who creates or handles classified documents.

faqs.q: Who has to complete this training?
faqs.a: Personnel who create, mark, or derivatively classify documents — generally the same audience required to take Derivative Classification training.

faqs.q: What's the difference between this and Derivative Classification training?
faqs.a: Derivative Classification training covers the decision of what should be classified and at what level; Marking Classified Information training covers how to correctly display that decision on the document itself — banner lines, portion marks, and the classification authority block.

faqs.q: Where is the official guidance for classification markings?
faqs.a: DoDM 5200.01, Volume 2, and the Information Security Oversight Office's (ISOO) marking guidance are the primary references behind this training.
